milestones.title: 01 Upload Finalizes Meeting
milestones.goal: A user uploads a recorded meeting and receives a finalized transcript, headline, summary, topics, talking points, and tasks without using live recording.
milestones.why: Upload finalization is the smallest shared proof of the meeting rebuild path. It establishes the canonical post-processing pipeline before live recording, recovery, notes, speakers, playback, or hardening depend on it.
milestones.included:
- User creates or selects a meeting and uploads one supported audio file.
- The uploaded source audio is persisted so the meeting can be rebuilt deterministically.
- The uploaded audio is transcribed into a final transcript.
- A final meeting headline, summary, topics, talking points, and extracted tasks are generated.
- The meeting finalization state is visible so the user can tell whether processing is pending, failed, or complete.
milestones.excluded:
- Live microphone capture or streaming transcript.
- Local browser durability, reconnect recovery, or background recording behaviour.
- User notes, live talking points, live task reconciliation, speaker assignment, synced playback, or recording hardening.
- Editing generated artifacts after finalization.

acceptance.text: User uploads an audio file to a meeting from the app.
The meeting shows a processing state while upload transcription and synthesis run.
The final transcript is visible after processing completes.
Headline, summary, topics, talking points, and tasks are visible on the finalized meeting.
Refreshing the page preserves the finalized artifacts and processing state.
Upload finalization failure leaves a visible failed state with enough diagnostic context for retry or support.
No live recording capability is required to complete this milestone.

milestones.title: 02 Reusable Task Components
milestones.goal: A single set of reusable task components powers full create, read, update, delete, and search on both the /tasks listing page and the meeting detail page, with consistent behaviour across surfaces.
milestones.why: Milestone 01 proves the finalization pipeline that produces tasks from uploaded audio. Before live recording layers draft tasks and reconciliation logic on top, the task surface itself must be consistent and fully functional. Building shared components now means every later milestone that touches tasks — live task capture, reconciliation, and review — inherits a stable, tested foundation rather than forking behaviour across surfaces.
milestones.included:
- A shared task component library used by both the `/tasks` page and the meeting detail tasks section.
- Full task CRUD on both surfaces: create, edit, toggle status (pending/completed), and delete with confirmation.
- Task search and filtering: text search across task content, filter by status (all/pending/completed), filter by assignment (all/my tasks/allocated).
- Meeting-scoped task views: the meeting detail page shows tasks scoped to that meeting with the same CRUD and filtering capabilities as the global tasks page.
- Sub-task display: sub-task summary (total/completed count) on parent tasks, with expandable sub-task list.
- Assignee management: a shared assignee picker component for assigning tasks to people.
- Due date management: a shared due date picker with contextual formatting (overdue, today, tomorrow, upcoming).
- Consistent empty, loading, and error states across both surfaces.
- Task metadata display: assignee avatar, due date badge, meeting link badge, and source indicator (user/system).
milestones.excluded:
- Live task extraction from streaming transcript or AI-generated draft tasks during recording.
- Task reconciliation logic between user-owned and system-generated tasks.
- Speaker-aware task assignment suggestions.
- Sub-task CRUD (display only; full sub-task management is out of scope).
- Task export, external integrations, or notification triggers.
- Drag-and-drop reordering or kanban-style views.
milestones.slices:

acceptance.text: The `/tasks` page and meeting detail tasks section render tasks using the same shared components.
User can create a task from both the `/tasks` page and the meeting detail page.
User can edit a task inline or via dialog from both surfaces.
User can toggle task status between pending and completed from both surfaces.
User can delete a task with confirmation from both surfaces.
User can search tasks by content text.
User can filter tasks by status and assignment category.
Meeting detail shows only tasks scoped to that meeting.
Task metadata (assignee, due date, meeting link, sub-task count) displays consistently across surfaces.
Loading, empty, and error states are consistent between both surfaces.

milestones.title: 03 Reusable Note Components
milestones.goal: A single set of reusable note components powers full create, read, update, delete, search, and context linking across the /notes listing page, meeting detail notes section, and people detail notes tab, with consistent behaviour across surfaces.
milestones.why: Notes are the first user-authored artifact that spans multiple surfaces — global listing, meeting context, and people context. Before live recording introduces autosaved meeting notes and the finalization pipeline must preserve them, the note surface itself must be consistent and fully functional. Shared components now mean the later live notes milestone inherits a stable editor, persistence model, and display rather than forking behaviour across surfaces.
milestones.included:
- A shared note component library used by the `/notes` page, meeting detail notes section, and people detail notes tab.
- Full note CRUD on all three surfaces: create with rich text editor, edit inline or via composer, and delete with confirmation.
- Note search: text search across note content and tags.
- Tag management: add, remove, and filter by tags with the shared tag picker.
- Context linking: link notes to a person or meeting via the shared context link picker, with the correct context pre-filled when creating from a meeting or person page.
- Meeting-scoped note views: the meeting detail page shows notes linked to that meeting with full CRUD capability.
- Person-scoped note views: the people detail page shows notes linked to that person with full CRUD capability.
- Rich text editing: the shared composer and editor support markdown shortcuts, formatting toolbar, and preview.
- Note card display: consistent card rendering with extracted title, excerpt, tags, context badge, and timestamp across all surfaces.
- Consistent empty, loading, and error states across all three surfaces.
milestones.excluded:
- Collaborative or shared notes between users.
- Autosave during live recording (addressed in the live notes milestone).
- Using notes as ML prompt context for synthesis.
- Note export, external sync, or notification triggers.
- Note versioning or revision history.
- Attachment support (images, files) within notes.

Meeting detail shows only notes linked to that meeting.
People detail shows only notes linked to that person.
Note cards display title, excerpt, tags, context badge, and timestamp consistently.
Loading, empty, and error states are consistent across all three surfaces.

milestones.title: 04 Live Transcript To Final Rebuild
milestones.goal: A user records live audio, sees a live transcript during the meeting, and stops recording to rebuild the same final artifacts through the finalization path proven by Milestone 01.
milestones.why: Live recording should not create a separate finalization model. After upload proves the rebuild path, live recording can focus on capture and streaming while stop hands the recorded audio into the same final transcript and synthesis pipeline.
milestones.included:
- Start and stop a live recording session from the meeting UI.
- Stream live audio from the browser to the backend processing path.
- Stream live transcript segments back to the user while recording continues.
- Persist the recorded audio source for final rebuild after stop.
- On stop, invoke the same finalization path proven in Milestone 01.
- Replace draft live transcript output with the final transcript and final meeting artifacts.
milestones.excluded:
- Offline-first OPFS durability, reconnect gap recovery, or degraded health surfaces beyond basic live failure states.
- Private notes, live talking points, live tasks, speaker labelling, playback review, or hardening policies.
- Divergent live-only final synthesis behaviour.
- Pause/resume or multi-device recording control.

Draft live transcript output is replaced by the final transcript when rebuild completes.
Final headline, summary, topics, talking points, and tasks match the final rebuild output.
A failed live stream or final rebuild leaves a visible recoverable state.

milestones.title: 05 Live Audio Durability Recovery
milestones.goal: A live recording remains durable across normal connectivity interruptions, with recoverable audio gaps and clear health or degraded states for the user.
milestones.why: Once live recording feeds the final rebuild path, the next risk is losing source audio before finalization. Durability and recovery must be proven before layering notes, insights, tasks, speakers, and playback on top of the recording session.
milestones.included:
- Buffer live audio locally using the agreed browser durability mechanism.
- Upload durable audio chunks to object storage as recording progresses.
- Recover upload gaps after reconnect when local durable chunks are still available.
- Show healthy, reconnecting, degraded, and failed recording states.
- Preserve enough source audio for final rebuild after transient network failures.
milestones.excluded:
- Private notes or generated live insights.
- Speaker assignment, playback review, or final artifact editing.
- Full hardening matrix for long sessions, no-audio detection, auto-stop, multi-tab guard, or browser capability gates.
- Cross-device continuation of the same recording.

Uploaded chunks are tracked durably in object storage.

Reconnect uploads locally buffered gaps when available.
Final rebuild includes recovered audio after a transient interruption.
Unrecoverable gaps are visible to the user and reflected in diagnostics.

milestones.title: 06 Live Notes
milestones.goal: A user can write private notes during a live recording, have them autosaved, and keep them attached to the meeting after finalization.
milestones.why: Durable live audio establishes that the recording session can survive instability. Notes are the first user-authored artifact layered onto the session and must prove autosave and preservation before generated live insights or task reconciliation add more mutable state.
milestones.included:
- Show a private notes surface during live recording.
- Autosave note edits while the recording is active.
- Preserve notes across refresh and finalization.
- Keep notes separate from generated transcript and synthesis output.
- Display notes in the finalized meeting review surface.
milestones.excluded:
- Collaborative notes, shared visibility controls, or rich-text editing.
- Generated talking points, task extraction, or speaker assignment.
- Using notes as ML prompt context for final synthesis.
- Export or external sync of notes.
milestones.slices:

milestones.title: 07 Live Talking Points
milestones.goal: A user sees draft talking points during a live meeting, then receives final talking points from the final rebuild after recording stops.
milestones.why: After the recording, finalization, durability, and user notes surfaces are stable, the system can safely add generated live insight previews without confusing them with final rebuilt artifacts.
milestones.included:
- Generate draft talking points from the live transcript while recording continues.
- Label live talking points as draft or provisional.
- Update draft talking points as more transcript context arrives.
- On finalization, replace draft talking points with final talking points from the rebuild path.
- Preserve private notes separately from generated talking points.
milestones.excluded:
- User task extraction or reconciliation.
- Speaker labelling, audio playback, or review-time transcript sync.
- Manual editing or pinning of talking points.
- Treating live draft talking points as final meeting output.

milestones.title: 08 Live Tasks And Reconciliation
milestones.goal: A user can work with live extracted tasks during a meeting, create or edit tasks manually, and have final task reconciliation preserve user-owned edits after rebuild.
milestones.why: Tasks introduce generated state that users can modify. They belong after live insights because reconciliation rules must distinguish draft machine output from user-owned task changes before final artifacts replace provisional ones.
milestones.included:
- Extract draft tasks from the live transcript during recording.
- Allow user task create, update, complete, and delete actions during the meeting.
- Track whether task fields are generated or user-owned.
- Reconcile final rebuilt tasks with live draft tasks and user edits after stop.
- Preserve user-created tasks and user-owned edits through finalization.
milestones.excluded:
- Speaker-aware assignment suggestions.
- External task export or integration with third-party systems.
- Complex dependency graphs, recurring tasks, or subtasks.
- Audio playback and click-to-seek review flows.

User edits are not overwritten by final generated task output.
Deleted user-owned tasks do not reappear from final reconciliation without an explicit conflict state.

milestones.title: 09 Speaker Labelling
milestones.goal: A user can assign transcript speaker labels to people, create missing people, and keep those assignments when the final transcript replaces provisional transcript output.
milestones.why: Speaker labels depend on transcript identity and final replacement semantics. They come after task reconciliation because both require user-owned metadata to survive regenerated ML output without being overwritten.
milestones.included:
- Show speaker labels on transcript turns or segments.
- Assign an existing person to a speaker label.
- Create a new person from the speaker assignment flow.
- Persist speaker-to-person assignments on the meeting.
- Preserve assignments when the final transcript replaces provisional live transcript output.
milestones.excluded:
- Automatic speaker identity recognition across meetings.
- Speaker-aware task assignment or summary rewriting.
- Contact enrichment, avatars, or organization directory sync.
- Audio playback review and synced transcript highlighting.

milestones.title: 10 Audio Playback And Review
milestones.goal: A user can review a finalized meeting with tabs, play the stored audio through a signed URL, see transcript highlighting synced to playback, and click transcript text to seek.
milestones.why: Playback relies on durable source audio, final transcript timestamps, and stable review artifacts. It follows speaker labelling so review can include the finalized transcript metadata users need to inspect.
milestones.included:
- Final review tabs for transcript, summary, talking points, tasks, notes, and playback-related review.
- Serve playable meeting audio through a time-limited signed URL.
- An audio player on the finalized meeting review screen.
- Highlight transcript content according to current playback time.
- Click transcript content to seek the audio player.
milestones.excluded:
- Download/export of audio or transcript.
- Editing transcript text from the playback review UI.
- Advanced waveform visualization or variable playback analytics.
- Recording hardening policies such as auto-stop, no-audio detection, and multi-tab guard.

milestones.title: 11 Recording Hardening
milestones.goal: A live recording behaves predictably under real-world browser and session constraints, with clear guards, automatic stops, capability gates, and diagnostics.
milestones.why: The core user value is proven before hardening so edge-case policy can be tested against complete recording, finalization, notes, insights, tasks, speakers, and playback behaviour rather than a partial flow.
milestones.included:
- Validate long recording session behaviour against the agreed duration target.
- Handle background tab behaviour with visible user guidance and diagnostics.
- Detect no-audio input and warn or stop according to policy.
- Auto-stop recordings when hard limits are reached.
- Prevent conflicting multi-tab recording control for the same user and meeting.
- Gate unsupported Safari or OPFS capability combinations with clear fallback messaging.
- Capture diagnostics for recording health, recovery, and failure investigation.
milestones.excluded:
- New user-visible meeting artifacts beyond the recording and review flow.
- Mobile-native recording support.
- Cross-device recording handoff.
- Enterprise compliance workflows or retention policy automation.

Background tab behaviour is visible and does not silently corrupt recording state.
No-audio input produces a warning or auto-stop according to policy.
Recording auto-stops when hard duration or health limits are reached.
A second tab cannot start or control a conflicting recording for the same meeting.
Unsupported Safari or OPFS capability combinations are gated before recording starts.
Diagnostics identify recording health, reconnects, degradation, and stop reasons.
